newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds ended lower, with bond traders blaming rising swap rates for Thursday's declines.
"The whole move came out of the swaps, swap (rates) are up massively. In addition there were practically no buyers," one Swiss cash bond trader said.

He added the drop appeared "more than a consolidation" after recent gains. "I think we are going down further," he said. He doubted the Swiss market would continue to outperform Bunds near-term, after the Swiss market gained recently relative to German bonds. The 10-year yield spread to Bunds narrowed on Thursday to 219 basis points from 222 on Wednesday.

But a London-based trader said the Swiss market still was attractive, at least versus the mark, which is viewed as the future anchor for the planned joint currency withhin European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).

In the short end, he added that last week some traders had apparently expected Swiss short term interest rates to start falling, but rates have stayed fairly steady, leading to a sudden surge in demand for liquidity.
"There is a bit of panic going on," the trader added.
